body:
It's a common pattern in asynchronous ruby worker patterns to be able to define default options for the definition using class methods. Coinbase's ruby temporal sdk allows for this, but temporalio's does not. 

For instance, configuring a retry policy for a specific activity should be possible, like so:

```ruby
class MyActivity < Temporalio::Activity::Definition
  retry_policy(
    initial_interval: 1,
    backoff_coefficient: 2.0,
    max_interval: 60,
    max_attempts: 10,
  )

  def execute
    # ... method body
  end
end
```

Otherwise, one has to specify the retry policy everywhere the activity is invoked explicitly, which is cumbersome. 

This should work for `Temporalio::Activity::Definition` and `Temporalio::Workflow::Definition`.

comments.body:
It is very intentional across all SDKs that retry policies are set at the callsite instead of the definition site. This represents how Temporal is built in that retry policy is a caller option. Many users invoke workflows or activities without having the definition present at all (e.g. across languages). In other situations, the actual definition that runs may be a different version of code from the one the caller is using and it would be improper for someone to, say, deploy their activity w/ new retry policy value and expect that callers automatically get it. It is important for user clarity that retry policy remain clearly a caller-only option and not try to hide that it is.

However, we do encourage users to feel free to set constants on their definitions and reference them, or create helpers for other callers that invoke the activities with a known set of retry policies (and/or timeouts and/or any other activity options).

Thanks @cretz  for the rapid response!

> It is important for user clarity that retry policy remain clearly a caller-only option and not try to hide that it is.

While I admit I have yet to fully grok Temporal, I can appreciate a sound and intentional architectural decision when I see one. Aside from retry policy, is the same logic applicable to things like `task_queue`, `start_to_close`, etc? I assume so, because of this:

> In other situations, the actual definition that runs may be a different version of code from the one the caller is using and it would be improper for someone to, say, deploy their activity w/ new retry policy value and expect that callers automatically get it. 

but just confirming!

> However, we do encourage users to feel free to set constants on their definitions and reference them, or create helpers for other callers that invoke the activities with a known set of retry policies (and/or timeouts and/or any other activity options).

So the way to understand this is that individual applications should define custom behavior layered on top, consistent within that application only, that can be used for ergo / convenience. Is that right?

> is the same logic applicable to things like task_queue, start_to_close, etc?

Yes, these are caller choices independent of the implementation

> So the way to understand this is that individual applications should define custom behavior layered on top, consistent within that application only, that can be used for ergo / convenience. Is that right?

I wouldn't necessarily say "should", but yes, this is the common pattern to for option sharing/reuse.

Haha, okay, fair enough. Thanks for clarifying. I'll find a pattern that strikes the appropriate balance of accuracy and ergo for us.
